_comment: Which model runs which phase, by tier — the one place to turn. Read by scripts/process/dispatch.py; measured by process_kpis.py models (telemetry module). Phases: brainstorm, plan, execute, review. Brainstorm requires tier >= 2 and owner approval before starting plan. A tier without an entry falls back to `default` per phase. `command` is the project's way to start a worker session (the default is Claude Code's CLI; with another harness, put its CLI here): {model} and {prompt} are substituted inside the argv this template splits into; the prompt is one argv element; {branch} and {issue} name the session where the harness labels sessions (Claude Code: `--remote-control={branch}` makes each worker visible in the Claude app — the `=` form, because the flag's optional name would otherwise eat the prompt). TRUST: this command runs on the machine that runs dispatch — a change here is a change to what the steward's host executes; review it like CI configuration. `env`: environment for worker sessions only, top-level and per phase (`phases.<phase>.env` wins) — e.g. `{"CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL": "sonnet"}` runs built-in subagents on a cheaper model; a worker-only advisor goes into `command` (Claude Code: `--settings '{"advisorModel":"opus"}'`); the owner's own sessions keep their settings; `PROCESS_*` is dispatch's own. `max_workers` caps concurrent dispatched sessions on this host. `worker_nice` (default 10, 0 = off): local workers start under `nice`, so the merge train keeps its CPU. `decision_channel`: how a worker reaches the steward live (e.g. `SendMessage to 'steward'`); the start prompt names it, so the steward's instructions there are not refused as a stranger's; {branch} and {issue} in it are filled as in `command` — default: none, reports and plan decisions carry communication; when set, report lifecycle and blocking events there too. `say_prompt`: a regex for the harness input line `dispatch.py say` checks (group 1 = what is still typed; default: a `>` prompt, maybe boxed). `runner`: `detached` (headless; a `-p` session needs its tool permissions granted in the project's settings or via --permission-mode, else it stops at the first gate) or `tmux` (each worker a window of tmux session `tmux_session` — interactive, a human can open it and `dispatch.py say` can type into it; use a non -p command then, e.g. `claude --model {model} --permission-mode acceptEdits {prompt}`; a fresh worktree may show a trust dialog on first start). `phases`: per-phase overrides — `{"review": {"command": "...", "runner": "detached", "remote": true}}`; `remote: true` means the session runs on another host (with `"runner": "tmux"` the hand-over command runs in a tmux window — for starters that need a terminal; `list` then shows a failed hand-over as HAND-OVER FAILED); `handover_id`: a regex that captures the other host's session id from what the hand-over printed (group 1; default: the first URL), shown by list, log and the tower (a cloud session, another machine): dispatch creates no worktree here, the command is the hand-over (it must exit 0 once the session is started; its stdout is kept), the branch must be on origin, and the worker reports with `--sync` so `tower.py --remote` sees it. Reviews are the natural remote phase: git-only, CPU-heavy, and a fresh clone on another host is independence for free. `transcripts`: a glob of the harness's session transcripts (JSONL), `{worktree}` substituted with each dispatched worktree of the issue — harness-specific, default none; `finish.py` and `process_kpis.py cost --issue N` sum their `output_tokens`, and say `not measured` without it. `classes`: a model per task class and phase (`[mechanical]`, `[design]` on a task line; unmarked is `standard`, which takes the tier) — consulted before the tier; `dispatch.py policy --class C` prints the row. A subagent spawn that names its model wins over the harness default; `classes` is where that name comes from (`docs/process/tower.md`). PROJECT CHOICES go into `docs/process/model-policy.local.json`, laid over this file mapping by mapping (`{"tiers": {"3": {"execute": "..."}}}` changes one cell): this file stays the template's, so a release's edits here still arrive.
